records.title: Docket 2026-138-E: comments on large-load additions
records.recordDate: Opened May 27, 2026
records.summary: The Public Service Commission docket is open to receive comments addressing large-load additions. The docket card is the place to verify current filings, orders, hearings and deadlines.
records.boundary: This is an electricity-regulation proceeding. It is not a permit to construct or operate a data center.
records.sourceLabel: South Carolina Public Service Commission

records.title: APS rate case: treatment of extra-high-load customers
records.recordDate: Hearing concluded July 7, 2026
records.summary: The Arizona Corporation Commission says the case includes proposed changes to APS's Extra High Load Factor, which applies to large-load users including data centers. A recommended order is expected before a Commission vote.
records.boundary: The rate case concerns utility terms and charges. It does not approve a data-center site or establish that a named project will operate.
records.sourceLabel: Arizona Corporation Commission

records.title: Bill 24-26E: proposed two-year building-permit moratorium
records.recordDate: Introduced May 12, 2026
records.summary: The introduced bill would prohibit the county Department of Permitting Services from issuing a building permit for a data center and would sunset two years after taking effect.
records.boundary: The source is an introduced bill and hearing record. It is not described here as enacted law.
records.sourceLabel: Montgomery County Council bill packet

records.title: Temporary pause on certain new hyperscale permits
records.recordDate: Announced July 14, 2026
records.summary: The governor's office says DEC will pause discretionary permits not already deemed complete while the state develops a generic environmental review and regulatory framework.
records.boundary: The announcement does not say that every data-center project or every local approval is prohibited.
records.sourceLabel: Office of Governor Kathy Hochul

records.title: Docket 55378: Q1 2026 large-load economic-development report
records.recordDate: Filed May 15, 2026
records.summary: The Georgia Public Service Commission record provides the public filing page and attachments for Georgia Power's quarterly large-load economic-development report.
records.boundary: The PSC record concerns regulated utility service. The Commission does not approve data-center construction, location or operation.
records.sourceLabel: Georgia Public Service Commission

records.title: Docket 6630-TE-113: very-large-customer tariff
records.recordDate: Open-meeting decision April 24, 2026
records.summary: The Wisconsin PSC described changes to a proposed tariff for very large customers and identifies 6630-TE-113 as the docket containing the proceeding's documents.
records.boundary: The linked release summarizes an open-meeting decision and says the final order controls. The PSC does not grant permits to build or operate data centers.
records.sourceLabel: Public Service Commission of Wisconsin

records.title: HB 3546: large-energy-use customer classification
records.recordDate: 2025 regular session
records.summary: The enacted measure directs the Public Utility Commission to create a service classification for large energy-use facilities and requires cost allocation and risk protections for other retail customers.
records.boundary: The law concerns utility service and cost allocation. It is not a siting approval or a facility inventory.
records.sourceLabel: Oregon Legislative Information System
